Party Entertainment

Kids party entertainers who run the whole party, not just a show

An all rounder entertainer is the safest booking most parents make. They arrive with a plan, hold a room full of children for an hour or two, and hand the party back to you in better shape than they found it.

A kids party entertainer is the person who takes the party off your hands. Not a performer who does a set and leaves, but a host who arrives early, reads the room, and keeps twenty over excited children moving in roughly the same direction for the length of the booking.

Most Australian entertainers work to a package rather than an hourly rate, and most packages bundle two or three skills. A typical booking might be games and music with face painting folded in, or a short magic set followed by balloon models and a dance off. That bundling is why an entertainer often costs less than booking the same elements separately.

Tell us the suburb, the date and your child's age and we will put your brief in front of entertainers who genuinely cover your area and are free on the day.

What you are booking

What a party entertainer package normally covers

Packages vary by performer, so treat the left column as the baseline and the right as the things worth asking about.

Usually included

  • Arrival ahead of the start time to set up and check the space
  • A structured run sheet of games matched to the age group
  • Portable speaker, music and any props the games need
  • Prizes or small giveaways for game winners
  • A managed cake and happy birthday moment
  • Public liability insurance and a certificate on request

Worth asking about

  • Whether face painting or balloons are inside the package or extra
  • Whether they bring a second performer for larger groups
  • What happens if the party runs long or rain moves it indoors
  • Power access, shade and the minimum floor space they need
  • Whether a Working with Children Check is held and can be sighted

The single biggest cause of a flat party is entertainment pitched at the wrong age. Use this as a starting point, then tell us the real ages in your brief.

Before you book

Five questions that separate a good booking from a gamble

Ask these before you pay a deposit. Any experienced entertainer will answer them without hesitating.

  1. What exactly happens in the first ten minutes? A confident answer here tells you they have a real run sheet rather than a bag of tricks.
  2. How many children is this package designed for, and what changes if more turn up?
  3. Do you hold public liability insurance and a Working with Children Check, and can I see both?
  4. What do you need from me on the day. Power, shade, a table, a clear indoor backup?
  5. What is your wet weather and cancellation policy, and when is the deposit refundable?
Kids Party House is a matching platform, not the entertainer. You book and pay the supplier directly, so their terms, insurance and cancellation policy are the ones that apply.

Getting the most from the booking

Three small decisions that change how the hour feels

The entertainer sets the tone, but the setup around them decides whether the party flows or stalls.

Start the entertainment 20 to 30 minutes in. Let the guests arrive, settle and burn off the first rush before anyone tries to run a game.
Put the cake after the entertainment, not before. Sugar plus a structured game does not mix, and the cake is a natural signal that the party is winding down.
Give them one clear space and one power point. Splitting children between a yard and a lounge room is what makes an entertainer lose the room.

Questions parents ask

Kids party entertainer questions

How long should a kids party entertainer stay?

Ninety minutes suits most parties for ages five and up. An hour works for three and four year olds, who tend to run out of concentration before the entertainer runs out of material. Two hours is worth it for a large group, a wide age range or a school hall, where the extra time gets used moving between activities rather than filling gaps.

How many children can one entertainer handle?

Most solo entertainers are comfortable with 10 to 30 children. Beyond that you either split the group into rotations or book a second performer, otherwise the children at the back spend the party waiting. If you are expecting more than 30, say so in your brief so quotes come back sized correctly.

What is the difference between an entertainer and a party host?

An entertainer performs. A host organises. An entertainer runs the games and the show, while a host also manages the schedule, the food timing, the cake moment and the parents. Plenty of suppliers do both. If the running of the day is what you want lifted, look at kids party hosts.

Do entertainers bring their own music and equipment?

Almost always. Expect a portable speaker, a playlist, props and prizes. What they usually need from you is a power point within reach, a shaded or indoor area, and somewhere to put a bag. Confirm this when you book, especially for a park where there may be no power.

Can I book an entertainer and a jumping castle together?

Yes, and it is one of the most common combinations we see. Put both in the same brief and quotes come back for the pair, which also means you are not coordinating two separate arrival times yourself. See jumping castle hire.

How far ahead do entertainers get booked out?

Four to six weeks is comfortable. Saturday mornings between October and March go first, and the fortnight before Christmas is the tightest run of the year. If your date is inside two weeks, send the brief anyway, because availability shifts constantly.
